name: Einstein-Dirac-Maxwell Wormhole
description: A static wormhole held open by an electric field and a pair of massless Dirac fields, the exact solution of Einstein-Dirac-Maxwell theory that Jose Luis Blázquez-Salcedo, Christian Knoll and Eugen Radu found in 2021. Its $g_{tt}$ is the extreme Reissner-Nordström black hole's, its charge exceeds its mass, and the electric field runs through the throat from one side to the other.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and $r_0$, $Q_e$, and $M$ are lengths. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Jose Luis Blázquez-Salcedo, Christian Knoll and Eugen Radu held this wormhole open with an electric field and a pair of Dirac fields, the waves of particles of spin one half, and in their words "without needing any form of exotic matter" [blazquez2021]. A wormhole a traveller could cross needs matter at its throat whose radial tension exceeds its energy density, a condition Michael Morris and Kip Thorne worked out in 1988, and they called such matter exotic [morris1988]. The wormholes that Homer Ellis and Kirill Bronnikov found independently in 1973 are held open by a scalar field whose kinetic term has the opposite of the usual sign [ellis1973, bronnikov1973]. Blázquez-Salcedo, Knoll and Radu set out to show that fermions need no such field [blazquez2021].¶The uncharged version came a year earlier, from Blázquez-Salcedo and Knoll, held open by pairs of massless Dirac fields alone [blazquez2020]. Its clocks all run at one rate, its mass is zero, and its throat is the sphere of areal radius $r_0$ [blazquez2020]. In the coordinate $x = \sqrt{1 - r_0/r}$ the two sides of the throat are $x > 0$ and $x < 0$, and the two far regions lie at $x = \pm 1$ [blazquez2020]. The density of the Dirac fields never dies away in those far regions, so the fields "cannot be normalized" to a fixed number of particles [blazquez2020]. With Radu they added the electric field, and when the fermions are massless and feel no electric force the equations solve exactly [blazquez2021]. That solution is this metric, and at $Q_e = 0$ it is the uncharged wormhole again [blazquez2021, blazquez2020].¶Seen from far away, the wormhole is a charged mass whose charge exceeds its mass [blazquez2021]. Its $g_{tt}$ is the extreme Reissner-Nordström black hole's, $-(1 - M/r)^2$, with the mass $M = 2Q_e^2r_0/(Q_e^2 + r_0^2)$ fixed by the charge $Q_e$ and the radius $r_0$ of the throat [blazquez2021]. As $Q_e$ grows to $r_0$ the metric becomes the extreme black hole's, with the Dirac fields gone [blazquez2021]. No charge sits anywhere: the lines of the electric field go in at one mouth and come out at the other, so an observer on one side measures one sign of charge and an observer on the other measures the opposite sign [blazquez2021]. Charge held this way by the topology of space is what John Wheeler and Charles Misner called "charge without charge" in 1957 [misner1957, blazquez2021]. All of the energy density belongs to the electric field, and the Dirac fields add only a radial tension, greatest at the throat and gone at $Q_e = r_0$ [bronnikovkim2003, blazquez2021].¶Eighteen years earlier Kirill Bronnikov and Sung-Won Kim had written down the same metric while looking for wormholes in a brane world, where our four dimensions are a surface in a fifth [bronnikovkim2003, bolokhov2021]. The fifth dimension reaches ours through a tidal stress whose trace vanishes, so the scalar curvature is zero, and their third example takes the extreme Reissner-Nordström $g_{tt}$ and solves for the rest, which gives this wormhole [bronnikovkim2003]. In the coordinate $u$ of their substitution $r = r_0 + u^2$, every component of the metric is an even function of $u$, and the two sides join smoothly at $u = 0$ [bronnikovkim2003]. The radius of the throat is the larger of $r_0$ and $Q_e^2/r_0$, which trade places as $Q_e$ passes $r_0$ [bronnikovkim2003]. The match was pointed out in 2021 by Sergey Bolokhov, Bronnikov, Serguey Krasnikov and Milena Skvortsova, who also wrote that "it would be better to say that Dirac spinor fields become exotic matter under certain circumstances" [bolokhov2021].¶Daine Danielson, Gautam Satishchandran, Robert Wald and Robert Weinbaum examined the numerical wormholes, those of massive, charged fermions [danielson2021]. Each had been built by solving the equations on one side of the throat and joining that half to its mirror image, and they proved that a join obeying the field equations has to be smooth to every order [danielson2021]. The joins were not smooth: the metric lacks a continuous third derivative at the throat, a shell of charge sits there, and the Dirac field has "a spurious source term" on it [danielson2021]. Their conclusion was that these wormholes "cannot be solutions to the EDM equations" [danielson2021].¶The trouble lay in the mirror symmetry, according to Roman Konoplya and Alexander Zhidenko: a wormhole the same on both sides needs the charge density of the fermions to change sign at the throat, "requiring coexistence of particle and antiparticles without annihilation" [konoplya2022]. Without the symmetry they found wormholes of the same theory with every field smooth through the throat, whose clocks far away on the two sides run at different rates [konoplya2022]. With uncharged fermions as light as neutrinos such a throat could be millimetres across [konoplya2022]. Can one of them last? Ben Kain's simulations of 2023 let the smooth wormholes evolve in time, and in every case he ran, black holes formed, joined through the wormhole, and light that crossed the throat stayed trapped inside a black hole [kain2023].

related.text: The general static wormhole a traveller could cross, with any redshift function $\Phi$ and shape function $b$. This one has $e^{\Phi} = 1 - M/r$ and $b = r_0 + Q_e^2/r_0 - Q_e^2/r$ [morris1988, blazquez2021].
Reissner and Nordström's charged black hole. At $Q_e = r_0$ this wormhole is its extreme member, $r_q = r_s/2 = r_0$, with the throat closed into the horizon [blazquez2021].

The wormhole of a scalar field whose kinetic term has the opposite of the usual sign, the kind of field Blázquez-Salcedo, Knoll and Radu set out to do without [ellis1973, bronnikov1973, blazquez2021].
Another static wormhole whose matter has no energy density, only a radial tension and a tangential pressure, as the Dirac fields of this one have [tsukamoto2020].

Visser's wormhole, with all of its matter in a thin shell at the throat. The numerical wormholes of massive, charged fermions turned out to carry a shell of charge at theirs [visser1989nuclphysb, danielson2021].

Einstein and Rosen's bridge of 1935, two sheets of space joined at a throat that is a horizon. Written in $u$ with $r = r_0 + u^2$, this wormhole joins its two sheets in the same way, with no horizon [einstein1935, bronnikovkim2003].

coordinates.name: Areal Radius

parameters.description: Areal radius of the throat, a length
Electric charge as a length, $Q_e^2 = Gq^2/(4\pi\epsilon_0c^4)$ for the charge $q$, with $0 \le Q_e < r_0$
Mass as a length, $GM_{\mathrm{ADM}}/c^2$ for the mass $M_{\mathrm{ADM}}$ seen far away on either side, never above $Q_e$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ on either side of the throat, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ the areal radius. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $s$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/ds$.

nonzero.value: -\dfrac{\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r\,r_0 - Q_e^2\right)\left(r^2\,r_0^4 - 2r^2\,r_0^2\,Q_e^2 + r^2\,Q_e^4 + r\,r_0^3\,Q_e^2 + r\,r_0\,Q_e^4 - 2r_0^2\,Q_e^4\right)}{r^6\,r_0^2\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)r - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}

coordinates.kretschmann: K = \dfrac{4Q_e^4\left(\left(4r_0\,r^2 - 5\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)r + 6r_0\,Q_e^2\right)^2 + 8\left(r - r_0\right)^2\left(r_0\,r - Q_e^2\right)^2\right)}{r^8\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)r - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)^2} + \dfrac{2\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)r - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)^2 + 4\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)r - r_0\,Q_e^2\right)^2}{r_0^2\,r^8}

nonzero.value: -\dfrac{\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r\,r_0 - Q_e^2\right)\left(r^2\,r_0^4 - 2r^2\,r_0^2\,Q_e^2 + r^2\,Q_e^4 + r\,r_0^3\,Q_e^2 + r\,r_0\,Q_e^4 - 2r_0^2\,Q_e^4\right)}{r^6\,r_0^2\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)r - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}

geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{2Q_e^2\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r\,r_0 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)r - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{r^5\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)r - 2r_0\,Q_e^2}{2r\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r\,r_0 - Q_e^2\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r\,r_0 - Q_e^2\right)}{r\,r_0}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r - r_0\right)\left(r\,r_0 - Q_e^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{r\,r_0}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Bronnikov-Kim

parameters.description: Areal radius of the throat, a length
Electric charge as a length, $Q_e^2 = Gq^2/(4\pi\epsilon_0c^4)$ for the charge $q$, with $0 \le Q_e < r_0$
Mass as a length, $GM_{\mathrm{ADM}}/c^2$ for the mass $M_{\mathrm{ADM}}$ seen far away on either side, never above $Q_e$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, u, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r = r_0 + u^2$ the areal radius, so $u$ carries the square root of a length and runs through the throat at $u = 0$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $s$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/ds$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{M}{r_0 + u^2}\right)^2c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{4r_0\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^2}{r_0^2 - Q_e^2 + r_0\,u^2}du^2 + \left(r_0 + u^2\right)^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)

nonzero.value: \dfrac{u\,Q_e^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^5}

\dfrac{4r_0\,Q_e^2\left(4u^4\,r_0 + 3u^2\,r_0^2 - 5u^2\,Q_e^2 - r_0^3 + r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^2}

-\dfrac{4r_0\,Q_e^2\left(4u^4\,r_0 + 3u^2\,r_0^2 - 5u^2\,Q_e^2 - r_0^3 + r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^2}

\dfrac{Q_e^2\left(4u^4\,r_0 + 3u^2\,r_0^2 - 5u^2\,Q_e^2 - r_0^3 + r_0\,Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^6}

-\dfrac{Q_e^2\left(4u^4\,r_0 + 3u^2\,r_0^2 - 5u^2\,Q_e^2 - r_0^3 + r_0\,Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^6}
-\dfrac{2u^2\,Q_e^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^6}
\dfrac{2u^2\,Q_e^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^6}
-\dfrac{2u^2\,Q_e^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^6}
\dfrac{2u^2\,Q_e^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^6}

-\dfrac{4r_0\,Q_e^2\left(4u^4\,r_0 + 3u^2\,r_0^2 - 5u^2\,Q_e^2 - r_0^3 + r_0\,Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^4}

\dfrac{4r_0\,Q_e^2\left(4u^4\,r_0 + 3u^2\,r_0^2 - 5u^2\,Q_e^2 - r_0^3 + r_0\,Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^4}

\dfrac{4r_0\,Q_e^2\left(4u^4\,r_0 + 3u^2\,r_0^2 - 5u^2\,Q_e^2 - r_0^3 + r_0\,Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^4}

-\dfrac{4r_0\,Q_e^2\left(4u^4\,r_0 + 3u^2\,r_0^2 - 5u^2\,Q_e^2 - r_0^3 + r_0\,Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^4}
\dfrac{2u^2\,Q_e^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^4}
-\dfrac{2u^2\,Q_e^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^4}
-\dfrac{2u^2\,Q_e^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^4}
\dfrac{2u^2\,Q_e^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^4}
\dfrac{2u^2\,Q_e^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^4}
-\dfrac{2u^2\,Q_e^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^4}
-\dfrac{2u^2\,Q_e^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^4}
\dfrac{2u^2\,Q_e^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^4}

geodesics: \ddot{u} + \dfrac{u\,Q_e^2\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right) - 2r_0\,Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2\left(r_0 + u^2\right)^5}\dot{t}^2 + \dfrac{u\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - 2Q_e^2\right)}{\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0 + u^2\right)}\dot{u}^2 - \dfrac{u\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)}{2r_0\left(r_0 + u^2\right)}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{u\left(u^2\,r_0 + r_0^2 - Q_e^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{2r_0\left(r_0 + u^2\right)}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Compact

parameters.description: Areal radius of the throat, a length
Electric charge as a length, $Q_e^2 = Gq^2/(4\pi\epsilon_0c^4)$ for the charge $q$, with $0 \le Q_e < r_0$
Mass as a length, $GM_{\mathrm{ADM}}/c^2$ for the mass $M_{\mathrm{ADM}}$ seen far away on either side, never above $Q_e$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $x$ dimensionless, and $r = r_0/(1 - x^2)$ the areal radius, so the throat is $x = 0$ and the two far ends are $x = \pm 1$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $s$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/ds$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{M\left(1 - x^2\right)}{r_0}\right)^2c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{4r_0^4}{\left(1 - x^2\right)^4\left(r_0^2 - Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)}dx^2 + \dfrac{r_0^2}{\left(1 - x^2\right)^2}\left(d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)

nonzero.value: \dfrac{x\,Q_e^2\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2 - 2Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)\left(1 - x^2\right)^4\left(r_0^2 - Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)}{r_0^4\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2}

\dfrac{4Q_e^2\left(6x^4\,Q_e^2 + 5x^2\,r_0^2 - 7x^2\,Q_e^2 - r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2 - 2Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)\left(1 - x^2\right)\left(r_0^2 - Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)}

-\dfrac{4Q_e^2\left(6x^4\,Q_e^2 + 5x^2\,r_0^2 - 7x^2\,Q_e^2 - r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)}{\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2 - 2Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)\left(1 - x^2\right)\left(r_0^2 - Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)}
\dfrac{Q_e^2\left(6x^4\,Q_e^2 + 5x^2\,r_0^2 - 7x^2\,Q_e^2 - r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2 - 2Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)\left(1 - x^2\right)^3}{r_0^4\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2}
-\dfrac{Q_e^2\left(6x^4\,Q_e^2 + 5x^2\,r_0^2 - 7x^2\,Q_e^2 - r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2 - 2Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)\left(1 - x^2\right)^3}{r_0^4\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2}
-\dfrac{2x^2\,Q_e^2\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2 - 2Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)\left(1 - x^2\right)^3\left(r_0^2 - Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)}{r_0^4\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2}
\dfrac{2x^2\,Q_e^2\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2 - 2Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)\left(1 - x^2\right)^3\left(r_0^2 - Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)}{r_0^4\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2}
-\dfrac{2x^2\,Q_e^2\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2 - 2Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)\left(1 - x^2\right)^3\left(r_0^2 - Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)}{r_0^4\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2}
\dfrac{2x^2\,Q_e^2\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2 - 2Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)\left(1 - x^2\right)^3\left(r_0^2 - Q_e^2\left(1 - x^2\right)\right)}{r_0^4\left(r_0^2 + Q_e^2\right)^2}
